'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Assassination of Ismail Haniyeh]]
****[[Hamas]] political leader [[Ismail Haniyeh]] is assassinated in [[Tehran]], [[Iran]], after attending the inauguration ceremony of [[President of Iran|Iranian president]] [[Masoud Pezeshkian]]. Hamas and Iran blame [[Israel]] for the assassination; however, the [[Thirty-seventh government of Israel|Israeli government]] officially declines to comment. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/31/life-of-defiance-ismail-haniyeh-hamas-political-boss-killed (Al Jazeera)] [https://apnews.com/article/iran-hamas-israel-30968a7acb31cd8b259de9650014b779 (AP)]
****[[Qatar]] and [[Egypt]] warn that peace negotiations are in jeopardy as a result of the assassination. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/qatar-pm-says-how-can-mediation-succeed-when-one-side-assassinates-negotiator-2024-07-31/ (Reuters)]
***[[Killing of journalists in the Gaza war]]
****[[Al Jazeera Arabic]] journalist [[Ismail al-Ghoul]] and his cameraman are killed in an Israeli [[airstrike]] while conducting a news broadcast near Ismail Haniyeh's home in the [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/31/al-jazeera-journalist-cameraman-killed-in-gaza-attack (Al Jazeera)]
**[[2024 Iran–Israel conflict]], [[Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)|Israel–Hezbollah conflict]]
***[[Killing of Fuad Shukr]]
****A source close to [[Hezbollah]] tells [[Agence France-Presse|AFP]] that the body of top commander [[Fuad Shukr]] has been recovered, nearly 24 hours after he was killed in an [[Israel]]i airstrike on southern [[Beirut]], [[Lebanon]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2024/07/31/body-of-hezbollah-s-commander-fuad-shukr-found-in-rubble-in-beirut (Al Arabiya)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/body-hezbollah-military-commander-found-beirut-rubble-two-security-sources-say-2024-07-31/ (Reuters)]
***One Israeli civilian killed in a Hezbollah rocket strike in northern Israel and Israeli airforce planes are fired at in Lebanese airspace.[https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/article-812530 (The Jerusalem Post)]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Battle of Tinzaouaten (2024)|Battle of Tinzaouaten]]
***[[Mali]] announces that it carried out joint airstrikes with [[Burkina Faso]] on insurgents in and around [[Tinzaouaten]]. The [[CSP-PSD]] says that a Burkinabé drone strike killed dozens of civilians. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/mali-strikes-rebels-who-killed-many-soldiers-russians-2024-07-31/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Siege of Mariupol]], [[Prisoners of war in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Prisoners of war in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Ukraine]] demands that [[Russia]] explain the death of [[Prisoners of war in the Russian invasion of Ukraine#Ukrainian prisoners of war|Ukrainian POW]] Oleksandr Ishchenko in Russian captivity, who was being [[Trial|tried]] with 21 other captured [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian troops]] for being part of the [[Azov Brigade]] that Russian prosecutors allege is [[Far-right politics in Ukraine|far-right]] affiliated. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-protests-against-death-azov-brigade-member-russian-captivity-2024-07-31/ (Reuters)]
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**At least 19 people are killed during a [[Suicide attack|suicide bombing]] by [[Boko Haram]] at a market in [[Konduga]], [[Borno State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://punchng.com/suicide-bomber-kills-many-in-borno-market/ (Punch)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2024 Manila Bay oil spill]]
**The [[Cavite]] provincial government in the [[Philippines]] declares a "[[State of emergency|state of calamity]]" after an [[oil spill]] from the sunk [[Oil tanker|MT]] ''Terra Nova'' ship reaches the shores of eight municipalities, requiring implementation of a no-catch zone and relief aid to be given to around 25,000 [[Fisherman|fishermen]]. [https://www.gmanetwork.com/regionaltv/news/103196/oil-spill-reaches-cavite-state-of-calamity-declared/story/ (GMA Network)]
**The ''Mirola 1'' oil tanker is discovered to have run aground near the coast of [[Bataan]], becoming the third vessel to cause an oil spill in [[Manila Bay]] in the past week. [https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/regions/915357/third-vessel-found-leaking-hazardous-material-off-bataan/story/ (GMA Network)]
*Strong thunderstorms and winds in eastern [[Nebraska]] cause significant destruction, causing widespread power outages in [[Lincoln, Nebraska|Lincoln]] and [[Omaha, Nebraska|Omaha]], the two largest cities in the state. [https://www.nytimes.com/2024/07/31/us/storms-omaha-nebraska.html (''The New York Times'')]
*One person is killed and at least 40 others are injured when a tent collapses in a [[windstorm]] at a [[Buddhist]] [[retreat (spiritual)|retreat]] in [[Busby, Alberta|Busby]], [[Alberta]], [[Canada]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/edmonton/1-dead-dozens-hurt-in-tent-collapse-at-buddhist-meditation-centre-near-edmonton-1.7281954 (CBC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Lukoil oil transit dispute]]
**[[Prime Minister of Slovakia|Slovak Prime Minister]] [[Robert Fico]] threatens to suspend [[Slovakia]]'s [[Diesel fuel|diesel]] exports to [[Ukraine]] if the Ukrainian government continues to suspend [[Pipeline|pipeline]] oil transport from [[Petroleum industry in Russia|Russian oil]] company [[Lukoil]], which Slovakia claims is causing a national [[Energy crisis|energy crisis]]. [https://kyivindependent.com/slovakias-fico-threatens-to-cut-off-diesel-supplies-to-ukraine-over-russian-oil-dispute/ (''The Kyiv Independent'')]
*[[United States–Georgia relations]]
**The [[United States]] pauses US$95 million in assistance to the country of [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] due to its government passing a [[2023–2024 Georgian protests#Bill|law on "foreign agents"]], which US officials referred to as "anti-democratic" and a "draconian measure to stifle dissent". [https://www.reuters.com/world/us-pause-95-million-assistance-georgian-government-blinken-says-2024-07-31/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Human trafficking]]
**[[Human trafficking in the United States]]
***[[Human trafficking in California]]
****Fourteen people are arrested in a [[sting operation]] by a joint task force at the [[San Diego Comic-Con]] in [[San Diego]], [[California]], United States, for participating in a [[sex trafficking]] network. Ten victims were recovered, including one teenager. [https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/comic-con-2024-human-trafficking-operation-14-arrests-1235963596/ (''The Hollywood Reporter'')]
**[[Human trafficking in Spain]]
***Twenty-six people are arrested by [[Spain|Spanish]] police in [[Madrid]], [[Málaga]], and [[Toledo, Spain|Toledo]] for operating a [[Sex trafficking|sex trafficking]] ring that abused over 600 women. 32 women were freed during the operation. [https://apnews.com/article/eu-spain-police-sex-abuse-6327a563efaa8266e350915c49750d6e (AP)]
*[[2024 United Kingdom riots]]
**[[Riot]]ing occurs in [[Hartlepool]], [[United Kingdom]], reportedly in response to the [[2024 Southport stabbing|Southport stabbing attack]]. At least eight people are arrested and a number of [[Cleveland Police]] officers are injured in the unrest. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c727p6dxrd2o (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2024 Summer Olympics]]
**[[Diving at the Summer Olympics]]
***[[China at the Summer Olympics|China]] surpasses the [[United States at the Summer Olympics|United States]] for the record of most gold medals in Olympic [[diving (sport)|diving]]. [https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/china-passes-united-states-most-gold-medals-olympic-diving (NBC News)]
**[[Guatemala at the 2024 Summer Olympics]]
***[[Adriana Ruano]] wins the [[gold medal]] in [[Shooting at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's trap|women's trap shooting]] to set a new [[List of Olympic records in shooting|Olympic record]] and win the first gold medal for [[Guatemala]] in Olympic history. [https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5671986/2024/07/31/adriana-ruano-oliva-olympics-womens-trap-shooting-guatemala-first-gold/ (''The New York Times'')]
**[[North Korea at the 2024 Summer Olympics]]
***[[Kim Mi-rae]] and [[Jo Jin-mi]] win the [[silver medal]] in [[Diving at the 2024 Summer Olympics#Women's events|Women's synchronized diving]], [[North Korea]]'s first medal in the sport. [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20240731010600315?section=sports/index (Yonhap News Agency)]
**[[Tennis at the 2024 Summer Olympics]]
***[[Novak Djokovic]] defeats [[Dominik Koepfer]] to advance to the quarterfinals of the [[Tennis at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's singles|Men's singles tournament]], becoming the only player to reach the quarterfinals four times, and the oldest quarterfinalist in [[Tennis at the Summer Olympics|Olympic tennis history]] at the age of 37. [https://www.thetennisgazette.com/news/novak-djokovic-has-broken-two-olympic-records-after-beating-dominik-koepfer-and-reaching-quarter-final/ (The Tennis Gazette)] [https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/tennis/story/paris-2024-novak-djokovic-scripts-history-four-olympic-quarterfinals-2574473-2024-07-31 (''India Today'')]
